name: Engine M2: tween compiler and presets
description: Compiles a layer's tweens and its enter, exit and loop presets onto the MotionClock's GSAP timeline, deterministically, through the TargetRef contract from M1. Tested on plain objects; no Pixi or Three needed.

userStories.title: compileTweens for numbers and degrees, plus primeTimeline
userStories.description: As an engine developer, I want tweens compiled to fromTo calls on the master timeline so that any seek order gives the same values.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md sections 'Tween compiler' and 'Determinism tests the compiler must pass', and tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/hooks/usePixiAnimation.tsx (the comments on immediateRender and overwrite).

Create engine/src/timeline/compile.ts exporting Resolve, CompileResult, compileTweens(tl, tweens, opts) and primeTimeline(tl, timeSec) for 'number' and 'deg' kinds: resolve keys, group by TargetRef.obj, read missing from values at compile time, convert degrees, add fromTo with immediateRender false at layerStart + at, use set for duration 0, never set overwrite.
Unresolvable target or property: push an error string naming the layer id, tween index and property, and skip that tween.
Create engine/src/timeline/compile.test.ts implementing every determinism test listed in the spec on plain objects with a MotionClock from engine/src/core/clock.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Tween at 1, duration 2, to { x: 100 } on { x: 0 } (layer start 0, ease 'none'): seek 0 -> 0, seek 2 -> 50, seek 3 -> 100, seek 0.5 -> 0, seek 2 -> 50
Two tweens on x ([0,1] 0->100 then [2,3] 100->0, ease 'none'): seek 2.5 -> 50, seek 0.5 -> 50, seek 2.5 -> 50
from { alpha: 0 } to { alpha: 1 } at 0: after primeTimeline(tl, 0), alpha is 0
to { rotation: 90 } with a 'deg' TargetRef ends at Math.PI / 2 (within 1e-9)
A tween whose resolve returns null is skipped and CompileResult.errors has one message containing the layer id and the property name
Layer start 2 and tween at 1 places the tween at timeline time 3
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Colour tweens, repeat and yoyo
userStories.description: As an author, I want to tween colours given as hex strings and repeat tweens so that fills, tints and lights can change colour over time.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md 'Tween compiler' step 3 (colour proxy) and engine/src/core/paths.ts (setColor, getColor).

Extend engine/src/timeline/compile.ts: 'color' kind tweens a proxy { v: fromHex } to { v: toHex } at the same time and duration, calling ref.setColor(proxy.v) on update; missing from uses ref.getColor(); duration 0 calls setColor once via set + onComplete or a callback at that time.
Pass repeat and yoyo through to GSAP for every kind.
Add tests to engine/src/timeline/compile.test.ts for colours, repeat and yoyo, and for a colour set (duration 0) before and after its time.
acceptanceCriteria: A colour tween '#000000' -> '#ffffff' over [0, 2] with ease 'none': at seek 1 setColor last received a grey whose channels are each 127 or 128
Seeking back to 0 after the colour tween sets '#000000' again
A tween of x 0 -> 10 over 1 s with repeat 1 and yoyo true is at 10 at t = 1 and back at 0 at t = 2
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: validateTargets: static check of every tween target against the allowlist
userStories.description: As an author, I want wrong tween targets reported at load time with a path so that a typo is found before playback.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md section 'Target paths' (the allowlist table).

Create engine/src/timeline/targets.ts exporting LAYER_PROPS (per layer type: the base props plus tint for image and fill for text and shape), CAMERA_PROPS, OBJECT_PROPS, LIGHT_PROPS and validateTargets(doc) returning Array<{ path: string; message: string }>.

validateTargets checks: the target form is allowed for the layer type (camera, object:, light:, postfx: only on three layers; filter: on any layer); the referenced id exists (objects, lights including key, fill, rim, ambient, filters, postFx); for layer, camera, object and light targets every to and from key is in the allowlist. Filter and postFx param names are not checked here (the compiler reports them).
Create engine/src/timeline/targets.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: A tween with target 'camera' on a text layer gives one error with path 'layers[0].tweens[0].target'
'object:nope' on a three layer without that object gives an error; 'light:key' is accepted on a three layer with no extra lights
to { 'rotation.w': 1 } on 'object:can' gives an error naming 'rotation.w'; to { 'rotation.y': 90, 'material.color': '#ff0000' } passes
All four m1 fixtures in engine/fixtures validate with zero errors
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Enter presets as pure Tween builders
userStories.description: As an author, I want named entrances (fades, slides, zoom, pop, rotate, drop) so that a layer can arrive well with one line of JSON.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md section 'Presets' and the enter rows of its table, then the matching effects in tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/utils/gsapEffects/ (fadeEffects.ts, slideEffects.ts, zoomEffects.ts, backEffects.ts, bounceEffects.ts, rotateEffects.ts, animationConfigs.ts) for curves and eases.

Create engine/src/timeline/presets.ts exporting PresetContext, PresetKind, PresetDef and a PRESETS record; implement every enter preset in the table as build(ctx, ref, at, duration) returning Tween objects (layer-local times, from and to values, eases), honouring ref.ease and ref.params overrides.

Create engine/src/timeline/presets.test.ts: for each enter preset, compile its tweens onto a clock against a plain object with the base values and assert the state at the start (off-base or transparent) and at the end (exactly the base values).
acceptanceCriteria: Every enter preset ends with x, y, alpha, rotation, scaleX and scaleY equal to ctx.base (within 1e-6) at at + duration
slideInLeft with size.width 300 and base x 500 starts at x 200 and alpha 0
popIn uses a back.out ease and starts at scale 0
A preset given ref.duration 2 ends at at + 2; with no ref.duration it uses defaultDuration from the table
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Exit presets
userStories.description: As an author, I want named exits so that a layer can leave cleanly before its end.
steps: Read the exit rows of the presets table in engine/docs/02-timeline.md and the matching FADE_OUT, ZOOM_OUT and slide-out effects in tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/utils/gsapEffects/.
Add fadeOut, fadeOutUp, fadeOutDown, slideOutLeft, slideOutRight and zoomOut to PRESETS in engine/src/timeline/presets.ts.
Add tests to engine/src/timeline/presets.test.ts: base state at the exit's start, gone (alpha 0) at its end.
acceptanceCriteria: Every exit preset starts at ctx.base values and ends with alpha 0
slideOutRight with size.width 300 and base x 500 ends at x 800
zoomOut ends with scaleX and scaleY at 0.3 x base
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)

userStories.title: Loop presets, placement and expandPresets (including 3D object loops)
userStories.description: As an author, I want spin, float, pulse and sway that fill the time between enter and exit and end at rest so that idle motion never pops.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md 'Presets' (placement rules, the spin, float, pulse and sway paragraphs, and 'Loop presets on 3D objects') and SPIN_360 plus the DEFAULT/MIN/MAX_LOOP_ROTATIONS_PER_SEC constants in tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/constants/animation.ts.
Add spin, float, pulse and sway to PRESETS following the exact tween shapes in the spec (n whole periods, yoyo with repeat 2n - 1, sway quarter/half/quarter).

Create expandPresets(layer, ctx) in engine/src/timeline/presets.ts: places enter at 0, exit at layerLength - exit duration, loop between them, retargets spin, float and sway to 'object:<id>' when ref.target is set (rotation.y, position.y with amplitude default 0.05, rotation.z), and returns { tweens, errors } (unknown preset, target on a non-loop preset).
Add tests: spin over a 10 s span at 0.25 turns per second, float ends at base, sway ends at base, n = 0 adds nothing, retargeting to an object.
acceptanceCriteria: A layer of length 10 with enter fadeIn (0.6 s), exit fadeOut (0.5 s) and loop spin at 0.25 turns/s: the loop tween starts at 0.6, covers 2 periods (8 s), and rotation at 8.6 is base + 720 degrees
float and sway leave the target exactly at base at the end of their span; pulse leaves scale at base
A loop span shorter than one period produces no tweens and no error
loop { name: 'spin', target: 'object:can' } produces tweens with target 'object:can' on 'rotation.y'; enter { name: 'fadeIn', target: 'object:can' } produces an error
turnsPerSecond 5 is clamped to 1
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Timeline public index and an end-to-end compile test on a fixture
userStories.description: As a runtime author (m7), I want one import for the timeline API and proof that a whole fixture compiles so that wiring it up is mechanical.
steps: Read engine/src/timeline/*.ts written in US-001 to US-006 and engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md step 7 of load(doc).
Create engine/src/timeline/index.ts re-exporting compileTweens, primeTimeline, Resolve, CompileResult, validateTargets, the allowlists, PRESETS, expandPresets and the preset types.

Create engine/src/timeline/fixture.test.ts: parse engine/fixtures/basic-2d.json, build a plain-object fake node per layer (x, y, alpha, rotation, scale { x, y }, a 'fill' colour holder) with a resolve built from LAYER_PROPS, expand presets with size 200x100, compile everything on a MotionClock, prime, and check values at three times.
acceptanceCriteria: fixture.test.ts compiles basic-2d.json with zero compile errors
For a layer in basic-2d.json with an enter preset, its fake node's alpha is 0 at the layer's start and equals its base alpha after the enter duration
Seeking the fixture to 40 %, then 0, then 40 % again gives identical values on every fake node
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; browser checks load assets from web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/README.md and the spec doc the story names before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.

Porting is allowed: read tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src (a read-only copy of the library, inside this repo) and copy what engine/docs/port-map.md says. Never edit anything under tmp/. Every ported file starts with `// Ported from reacthub-pixitweenjs <path> (MIT).` and is cleaned up to strict TypeScript.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore` under engine/. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.
engine/ must not import from web/, server/, shared/, `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `@pixi/react` or `@react-three/*`. Only the web stub files listed in metadata.sharedEdits may import engine/.

Do not touch the director app: nothing under server/, shared/, web/src/ (except the stub files under web/ listed in metadata.sharedEdits) or the existing e2e/ specs. Config files only as listed in metadata.sharedEdits.
Everything you build goes under engine/ (src/, fixtures/, lab/, e2e/, docs/). Edit only the files named in the story's steps and their tests, plus the small edits listed in metadata.sharedEdits.

Determinism: no Math.random, Date.now or performance.now in anything that affects pixels; no GSAP `overwrite`, no `immediateRender: true`, no infinite `repeat` (engine/docs/02-timeline.md, determinism rules).
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic and object construction; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.
Do not add a dependency the spec does not name (`postprocessing` and `@types/three` are already declared).

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/engine/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server the owner runs on http://localhost:5173 (do not start another on a different port); if it is not running, run `npm run engine:e2e` instead.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

ui: Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
